full_judgment: 11. On the other hand Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 1-5 opposing the Rule submits that in the column of the possession in plot no. 227 of C.S. khatian no. 705 it has been articulated clearly that Afil Uddin and Keamuddin had been possessing the said land exclusively and C S. record of right has a presumption as to its genuineness which has not been rebutted by the defendants in any way. The defendants in their written statement very strongly asserted that Azibor, Damini and Rasik had been also residing in the land of plot no. 227 along with Afil Uddin and Keamuddin but this assertion of the defendants has not been proved in any way. The trial Court on due consideration of the evidence and other materials on record found the title and, possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land but also opined that since the plaintiffs had been ousted from a certain portion of the suit land during the pendency of the suit, so it will not be proper to pass a decree for permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiffs but the Appellate Court below relying on the decision of 35 DLR (AD) 43, 47 DLR 170 and 39 DLR 23 rightly held that the right of the parties should be determined at the time of filing of the suit and since after filing of the suit on 7.1.1997 the defendants had entered into possession forcibly in a portion of the suit land on 17.1.1997 the Appellate Court below rightly decreed the suit with a direction to surrender the possession by the defendants in favour of the plaintiffs.The learned Advocate also relying on the decisions of the case of Zamini Bala Vs. Abdul Aziz 10 MLR 25, submits that if a party is dispossessed from the suit land during the pendency of a proceeding, the Court must restore his possession. So the Appellate Court did not commit any error of law and fact in decreeing the suit and as such the judgment of the Appellate Court below did not call for any interference from the this court.
